name: Modern rules
author: DecompRecomp
description: Rules from the later games: one card drawn a turn after the opening five, a hand of up to ten kept to six at the end of a turn, turn phases with a Main Phase 2 as in the GX games, no card lost to a fusion that does not work, and Treasure Trickster, a spell that draws two. Needs Extra hand plays.

settings.label: Playing a card is optional
settings.description: START in the first hand of a turn plays no card and goes on to the field, as in the later games. Without it a full field with nothing that fuses would leave no legal play.

settings.label: Phases like the GX games
settings.description: START opens a menu of the next phases: from the hand (Main Phase 1) the Battle Phase or the End Phase; from the field the Main Phase 2, to play from the hand again after attacking, or the End Phase. The CPU plays as before.

settings.label: Draw one card a turn
settings.description: Each side opens with five cards, then draws one a turn (none on the first turn of the side that goes first). The hand holds up to ten. Off refills the hand to five each turn, as on the disc.

settings.label: Hand limit at the end of a turn
settings.description: With one card drawn a turn: a side ending its turn with more cards discards down to this many. The player picks them; the CPU throws away its weakest. 0 turns the limit off.

settings.label: Keep cards a fusion cannot use
settings.description: Cards put onto a monster must fuse with it or equip it, and marked cards must all fuse or equip in that order, so no card is thrown away. The player's confirm is refused; the CPU plays elsewhere, or no card.

settings.label: Treasure Trickster draws two
settings.description: Using Treasure Trickster draws two cards and brings the hand back up. Cards that do not fit in the hand wait for the next draw. The CPU uses it too.
